title: The self-duality conjecture for finite LR-structures
statement:
Let $(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ be a finite LR-structure, and let $\operatorname{Aut}^+(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ denote its orientation-preserving automorphism group. The LR-structure is **self-dual** when an automorphism of $\Gamma$ interchanges its two distinguished sets of cycles, $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{R}$. **The self-duality conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Aut}^+(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})<\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma),
$$

then $(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ is self-dual. This conjecture asserts that, for a finite LR-structure, the equality of the lengths of the cycles in $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{R}$—known to be necessary for self-duality under this hypothesis—is also sufficient. The claim was posed as Conjecture 8.1 in the cited source; the material provided does not state whether it has been resolved.
source_name: Marston Conder, Luke Morgan and Primož Potočnik, “Resolution of a conjecture about linking ring structures”, arXiv:2305.04261 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04261

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).
